statement: Definitions and the axioms actually required. Let $\D:\Cat_{\U}^{\mathrm{coop}}\to\mathrm{CAT}_{\V}$ be a prederivator. For a small category $A$, let $\LC_\D(A)$ be the full subcategory of $\D(A)$ on objects whose underlying presheaf $A^{\op}\to\D(e)$ sends every arrow to an isomorphism. If $f:A\to B$, restriction gives a functor $f^*:\LC_\D(B)\to\LC_\D(A)$. We define $\Wlc$ by this functor being an equivalence and $\Wone$ by its being fully faithful. Writing $p:A\to e$, $q:B\to e$, we define $\Wc$ by bijectivity of \[ \Hom_{\D(B)}(q^*M,q^*N)\longrightarrow \Hom_{\D(A)}(p^*M,p^*N)\qquad(M,N\in\D(e)). \tag{A.1.1} \] If all restrictions have adjoints $f_!\dashv f^*\dashv f_*$, we define $\Wcoh$, respectively $\Whom$, by invertibility, for every $F\in\LC_\D(B)$, of the specified comparison \[ q_*F\longrightarrow p_*f^*F, \qquad p_!f^*F\longrightarrow q_!F \quad\text{in }\D(e). \tag{A.1.2} \] The first map is induced by the unit $F\to f_*f^*F$; the second by the counit $f_!f^*F\to F$. The definitions require no enhancement.
notes: Definitions for a prederivator; Der1--4 and exact presheaf variance separately stated. No strongness assumed.

statement: The inclusion chain and its two separate last arrows. For a prederivator with the adjoints of A.1, \[ \Wlc\subseteq\Wone\subseteq \Wcoh\cap\Whom\subseteq\Wc. \tag{A.2.1} \] In fact each of $\Wcoh$ and $\Whom$ is separately contained in $\Wc$. For a derivator, $\Winfty\subseteq\Wlc$.
notes: Both local (co)homological classes separately imply constant equivalence; all-derivator first inclusion.

statement: What happens for a map to the point. For every prederivator and every $A$, \[ (A\to e)\in\Wc\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (A\to e)\in\Wone. \tag{A.3.1} \] Consequently the claim in the CATHOT addendum that an acyclic-group projection $BA\to e$ is a constant-coefficient equivalence but is not 1-complete is false.
notes: Corrects the reversed acyclic-group projection example for every prederivator, including the empty source.

statement: Closure properties that follow without descent. For any prederivator, $\Wc$ and $\Wlc$ contain identities and are closed under composition, two-out-of-three, and retracts of arrows. The class $\Wone$ contains identities, is closed under composition and retracts, and satisfies the cancellation rule \[ f\in\Wone,\quad gf\in\Wone\quad\Longrightarrow\quad g\in\Wone. \tag{A.4.1} \] With adjoints, $\Wcoh$ and $\Whom$ have these latter closure properties too. The missing two-out-of-three implication for these three intermediate classes is false even for a represented derivator.
notes: Distinguishes full two-out-of-three from the single valid cancellation rule.

statement: Two-out-of-three for 1-completeness. The assertion that $\Wone$ is a fundamental localizer for every derivator is false. The same obstruction applies to $\Wcoh$ and $\Whom$.
notes: Complete C2 category and regular action; code/A5_finite_counterexample.py and output.

statement: Locally constant coefficient derivators and shifts. For every derivator $\D$ and small $A$, the prescription \[ \mathbb L_A(I)= \{F\in\D(A\times I):F\text{ is locally constant in the }A \text{ direction}\} \tag{A.6.1} \] defines a derivator. Its inclusion in $\D^{A}$ has both adjoints as morphisms of derivators. Restriction along $f:A\to B$ gives a morphism $\mathbb L_B\to\mathbb L_A$ with both adjoints. It is fully faithful, or an equivalence, at every shape $I$ if and only if it is so at $e$.
notes: Locally constant shifted derivators; unit/counit and Der2 transfer the specified ordinary restriction to every shape.

statement: Finite products, coproducts, opposites, and a limit. For a derivator, all five classes are invariant under natural transformations between the indexing functors and under passage to opposite functors. They are closed under finite products of arrows. The classes $\Wlc$, $\Wone$, $\Wcoh$, and $\Whom$ satisfy the disjoint-union equivalence \[ \coprod_{j\in J}f_j\in\W \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad (\forall j)\ f_j\in\W \tag{A.7.1} \] for every small family. For $\Wc$ only the right-to-left implication holds in this generality; its converse is false. There is no general closure under infinite products of arrows, even for $\Winfty$ or the set-valued classes.
notes: Natural twisted-arrow span proves same-D opposite invariance. Finite products only; alternating fences refute infinite products. Constant class lacks reverse sum implication.

statement: What the ordinary-category comparison does prove with an enhancement. If $\mathcal C$ has all small limits and colimits, then \[ \LC_{\D_{\mathcal C}}(A)\simeq \Ho\Fun(BA,\mathcal C). \tag{A.8.1} \] For the specified restriction map, equivalence or full faithfulness on these homotopy categories is equivalent to the corresponding infinity-categorical property.
notes: Full faithfulness/equivalence of a specified adjoint restriction, not arbitrary equivalence of homotopy categories.

statement: Absolute Theorem A for every derivator. For every derivator $\D$, the class $\Wlc$ is weakly saturated, contains the categories with a terminal object, and satisfies the absolute Theorem A: if $u:A\to B$ and every $A/b\to e$ belongs to $\Wlc$, then $u\in\Wlc$. The constant-coefficient class $\Wc$ is a fundamental localizer, including the relative Theorem A. The class $\Wone$ need not be a localizer, by A.5.
notes: Absolute Theorem A holds for all derivators; constant class is fundamental by the checked Cisinski result.

statement: Relative Theorem A with an infinity-category enhancement. Let $\mathcal C$ be a complete and cocomplete infinity-category, with the universe bounds of the conventions. Then $\W^{\mathrm{lc}}_{\mathcal C}$ is a fundamental localizer. In particular, for a morphism $u:A\to B$ over a small category $S$, the hypotheses \[ (A/s\longrightarrow B/s)\in\W^{\mathrm{lc}}_{\mathcal C} \quad(s\in S) \tag{B.2.1} \] imply that the specified restriction $\Fun(BB,\mathcal C)\to\Fun(BA,\mathcal C)$ is an equivalence of infinity-categories.
notes: Enhanced Grothendieck homotopy-colimit proof; equivalence and fully faithful versions both proved.

statement: Relative Theorem A for an arbitrary derivator. Let $\D$ satisfy Der~1--4 in the presheaf convention of A.1, on all $\U$-small categories. Let $A\xrightarrow{u}B\xrightarrow{q}S$ be functors of $\U$-small categories and put $p=qu$. If, for every $s\in S$, the specified restriction \[ (u/s)^*:\LC_\D(B/s)\longrightarrow\LC_\D(A/s) \tag{B.3.1} \] is an equivalence, then $u^*:\LC_\D(B)\to\LC_\D(A)$ is an equivalence. If every restriction in (B.3.1) is fully faithful, then $u^*$ is fully faithful. Both conclusions also hold for a map of Grothendieck opfibrations preserving cocartesian arrows when the corresponding restriction on every strict fiber is, respectively, an equivalence or fully faithful. Consequently $\Wlc$ is a fundamental localizer for every such derivator, while $\Wone$ satisfies relative Theorem A despite its failure of two-out-of-three in A.5. The statement concerns the ordinary categories $\LC_\D(-)$ themselves; neither an infinity-categorical presentation nor strongness of $\D$ is required.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: PartB arbitrary derivator descent; D.11; Lead1
notes: All Der1--4 derivators. Partial LC projectors, cocartesian-compatible maps, fibrewise Kan and unit/counit detection; no enhancement or Der5.

statement: Accessibility for all computed coefficient theories. For every $\U$-presentable enhanced coefficient category, and in particular for the derivators of sets, groupoids, $r$-types ($r\geq0$), spaces, $D(k)$ for a small associative unital ring $k$, spectra, and $L_E\Sp$ for a small spectrum $E$, the constant and $2$-complete classes are set-generated fundamental localizers. They also satisfy the literal accessibility condition Loc~(9) of Chapter XVI ms.~75--79: as full subcategories of $\Cat^{[1]}$, they are generated under sufficiently filtered colimits by a small family of bounded-cardinality arrows. For the listed concrete coefficient theories the intermediate classes are accessible full subcategories of $\Cat^{[1]}$ as well; this does not turn them into fundamental localizers when two-out-of-three fails. No large-cardinal principle is used for these coefficient theories.
notes: Set generation and literal arrow-category accessibility proved for constant/LC classes of all presentable coefficients; concrete intermediate classes also accessible. Corrects subcategory-order transcription.

statement: Sums, components, direct excision, and filtered colimits. For every derivator, $\Wlc$ satisfies the full disjoint-union axiom Loc~(4). It satisfies Loc~(5), namely $\Wlc\subseteq\W_0$, exactly when $\D(e)$ is not equivalent to the terminal category. For every derivator it also satisfies the direct Mayer--Vietoris axiom Loc~(6a) and the filtered-colimit axiom Loc~(8). The class $\Wone$ satisfies Loc~(4), Loc~(6a), and Loc~(8) for every derivator, despite its possible failure of two-out-of-three. For arbitrary $\D$, it satisfies Loc~(5) exactly when $\D(e)$ is not a preorder up to equivalence. For arbitrary $\D$, the constant class $\Wc$ satisfies Loc~(6a) and Loc~(8); it satisfies Loc~(5) exactly under the nonthinness condition G.2, and need not satisfy the reverse implication in Loc~(4).
notes: Includes arbitrary-D W1 descent and filtered-colimit closure; nonthinness is exact component criterion for W1 and constant classes.

statement: The reverse Mayer--Vietoris axioms. For a derivator $\D$ with $\D(e)\not\simeq e$, the class $\Wlc$ satisfies neither Loc~(6b) nor Loc~(6c) of Chapter XVI. If $\D(e)\simeq e$, all arrows belong to $\Wlc$ and both axioms hold. For $\Wone$ of a nontrivial derivator, Loc~(6b) always fails, whereas Loc~(6c) holds exactly when $\D(e)$ is a preorder up to equivalence. Thus the unqualified Loc~(6), which includes Loc~(6b), fails for every nontrivial coefficient theory, even for spaces and ordinary weak homotopy equivalences. In contrast, each constant homology localizer $W_E$ satisfies all three Mayer--Vietoris implications Loc~(6a,b,c).
notes: Loc(6b) and Loc(6c) both fail for Wlc of every nontrivial derivator; both hold for the trivial derivator. All constant spectrum-homology localizers satisfy Loc(6a,b,c). For W1, 6b fails for every nontrivial derivator; 6c holds exactly for thin point coefficients.

statement: Classification of the fibration axioms. Let $W$ be a fundamental localizer with $W\subseteq W_0$. Define $\mathcal F_W$ to be the class of Grothendieck fibrations whose transport functors belong to $W$, and define $\operatorname{Fib}_W$ by preservation of all $W$-equivalences under strict categorical pullback. Then each of Loc~(7a), Loc~(7b) and Loc~(7c) holds if and only if $W=W_\infty$. In particular this applies to $W=\Wlc$ for every nontrivial derivator, by B.3 and G.1. For the trivial derivator all three axioms hold. If $W$ is accessible, Loc~(7F), with the manuscript's class $\operatorname{Fib}_W$, holds if and only if $W$ is proper, equivalently if and only if it is generated as a fundamental localizer by a set of projections $A\to e$. For a nonzero associative unital ring $k$ this specializes to the complete classification \[ \begin{split} \operatorname{Loc}(7F)\text{ for }W_{D(k)}^{\mathrm{lc}} &\Longleftrightarrow \text{no rational prime is invertible in }k\\ &\Longleftrightarrow W_{D(k)}^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_\infty. \end{split} \tag{B.7.1} \] The constant $k$-homology localizer satisfies none of Loc~(7a,b,c,F), for every nonzero $k$. For $\Wone$, which need not be a localizer, Loc~(7c) nevertheless holds for every derivator. With the enhancement of C.2, Loc~(7a) and the factorization assertion of Loc~(7F) hold as well; Loc~(7b) fails for sets, groupoids, every finite $r$-type theory, every nonzero $D(k)$, every nonzero $L_E\Sp$, and every nontrivial thin coefficient theory. These facts do not make $\Wone$ the weak-equivalence class of a Brown category.
notes: For a nontrivial fundamental localizer, each of Loc(7a,b,c) holds exactly for Winfty. For an accessible fundamental localizer, Loc(7F) is equivalent to properness and to aspherical generation. For nonzero unital k, Wlc_D(k) satisfies 7F exactly when no prime is invertible in k, equivalently exactly when it equals Winfty. Constant Hk satisfies none of 7a,b,c,F. For W1, 7c holds for all derivators, while enhancement proves 7a and the 7F factorization assertion. 7b fails for the listed nontrivial truncated, stable, and thin theories; spaces give Winfty. For a general spectrum E not evaluated here, is Wlc_L_E Sp equal to its aspherical core? This is exactly the remaining 7F question. For an arbitrary unenhanced derivator whose Wlc accessibility has not been established, 7F implies aspherical generation but its converse is not asserted. For arbitrary unenhanced derivators, W1 versions of 7a and the factorization assertion of 7F remain unproved; the enhanced proofs use Wcoh=W1 and the homotopy-fibre criterion, respectively. Literal 7c is proved in full generality.

statement: The sphere test, without accessibility. For every fundamental localizer $\W$ and every integer $n\geq0$, \[ \W_n\subseteq\W \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \bigl(\Delta/\partial\Delta^{n+2}\longrightarrow e\bigr)\in\W. \tag{B.8.1} \] No accessibility hypothesis is needed. In particular, this applies to $\Wlc$ for every derivator, by B.3. For $\mathcal C=\mathcal S_{\leq r}$ it holds exactly when $n\geq r+1$. For $\mathcal C=D(k)$ with $k\ne0$, or for ordinary spectra, it holds for no finite $n$.
depends_on: B.3; C.4; C.7; C.10; Cisinski2006 Prop9.2.17
notes: Sphere test has no accessibility hypothesis; applied to every derivator's locally constant localizer.

statement: An acyclic map is an epimorphism in the unpointed homotopy category. Let $t:X\to Y$ be a map of small CW spaces whose homotopy fibres are integrally acyclic, where ``acyclic'' includes nonempty and connected. Then for every small space $Z$ the map of unpointed homotopy classes \[ [Y,Z]\longrightarrow[X,Z] \tag{B.9.1} \] induced by $t$ is injective. The homotopy codiagonal $c:Y\cup_X^hY\to Y$ is a weak homotopy equivalence.
notes: Unpointed homotopy category; double homotopy pushout proves epimorphism and does not confuse it with equivalence.

statement: Acyclic simple overgroups of controlled cardinality. Let $H$ be a small group and let $\lambda$ be an infinite small cardinal with $\lambda\geq|H|$. There is an embedding $H\hookrightarrow A$ into a nonabelian simple integrally acyclic group with $|A|=\lambda$. Consequently, if $\lambda>\mu$, every homomorphism $A\to L$ to a group of cardinality at most $\mu$ is trivial.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: CATHOT BC B.6; cardinal Kan-Thurston lead
notes: Full simultaneous HNN and mitosis construction with embedding, acyclicity, simplicity, and cardinal control.

statement: The cardinal-controlled Kan--Thurston statement. Let $Y$ be a connected $\U$-small CW complex and let $\mu$ be a cardinal belonging to $\U$. There are a $\U$-small group $G$ and an acyclic map $t:BG\to Y$ such that $\phi=\pi_1(t):G\twoheadrightarrow\pi_1Y$ is onto, its kernel $P$ is perfect, and every homomorphism $G\to L$ with $|L|\leq\mu$ vanishes on $P$. Base points are chosen only to write $\phi$; acyclicity and the conclusion about the normal subgroup do not depend on their choice.
notes: Small CW spaces; arbitrary bound mu; aspherical replacement, local-coefficient homology isomorphism, perfect kernel, and small-group invisibility.

statement: Small ind-objects modulo natural transformations see at most one-types. Let $\mathcal H$ be the category of $\U$-small categories whose morphisms are functors modulo zigzags of natural transformations. Let $I$ be a nonempty $\U$-small filtered category, and let $K:I\to\mathcal H$ be a diagram, represented by categories $K_i$. Suppose the presheaf \[ H_K(X)=\colim_{i\in I}\Hom_{\mathcal H}(X,K_i) =\colim_i\pi_0\Fun(X,K_i) \tag{B.12.1} \] sends every functor in $\Winfty$ to a bijection. Then it sends every functor in $\W_1$ to a bijection. The specified unit of the reflector induces an isomorphism \[ (K_i)_{i\in I}\longrightarrow(\Pi_1K_i)_{i\in I} \quad\hbox{in }\operatorname{Ind}_{\U}(\mathcal H). \tag{B.12.2} \] In particular the small-index version of CATHOT E.17 is settled, with its original indexing category unchanged.
notes: Every U-small filtered ind-object satisfying stated W_infinity invariance has invertible Ind(Pi1) unit. Uniform cardinal bound; canonical localization comparison; no infinite-product/pi0 swap.

statement: Accessibility with only the abstract derivator axioms. For an arbitrary derivator $\D:\Cat_\U^{\mathrm{coop}}\to\mathrm{CAT}_\V$ satisfying Der~1--4, must $\Wlc$ be generated by a $\U$-small set of functors as a fundamental localizer? Must its full subcategory of $\Cat_\U^{[1]}$ satisfy the literal Loc~(9)? We likewise leave the corresponding accessibility assertion for $\Wc$ and the literal accessibility assertion for $\Wone$ unresolved in this full generality. B.4 answers the first two questions positively for every $\U$-presentable enhanced coefficient category, and answers all three for each concrete coefficient theory in Part C.
notes: Bare-derivator set-generation and literal accessibility not established; W1 accessibility also unproved here for general presentable coefficients outside the concrete families. Vopenka conditional for fundamental classes, not assumed; no explicit counterexample.

statement: The remaining general fibration questions. For an arbitrary Der~1--4 derivator without an enhancement, we leave unresolved whether every Grothendieck fibration whose transports belong to $\Wone$ universally preserves $\Wone$ under strict pullback, and whether every small functor factors as a member of $\Wone$ followed by such a universally $\Wone$-preserving map. These are respectively literal Loc~(7a) and the factorization assertion of Loc~(7F); Loc~(7c) is proved in B.7. For the accessible localizer $W^{\mathrm{lc}}_{L_E\Sp}$ of a general nonzero spectrum $E$, we also leave its properness, equivalently its Loc~(7F), unevaluated beyond the cases proved in B.7.
notes: Bare-D W1 7a/factorization gap; arbitrary-spectrum LC properness criterion exact but not evaluated already for K(1). Not a literature-wide openness claim.

statement: Ordinary full faithfulness detects the enhanced restriction. For every map $v:S\to T$, the functor $\Ho(v^*):\Ho\Fun(T,\mathcal C)\to\Ho\Fun(S,\mathcal C)$ is fully faithful if and only if $v^*$ is fully faithful as an $\infty$-functor. It is an equivalence if and only if $v^*$ is an equivalence of $\infty$-categories.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: I ms.99-100; Part B enhancement question
notes: Cotensors by all small spaces supply the required mapping-space tests.

statement: The middle three classes coincide for enhanced coefficients. For the above coefficient theory, put $F_y=S\times_T^h\{y\}$ for each point $y$ of $T$. The following conditions on $v$ are equivalent: \[ v\in W_{\mathcal C}^{1},\qquad v\in W_{\mathcal C}^{\mathrm{coh}},\qquad v\in W_{\mathcal C}^{\mathrm{hom}},\qquad F_y\otimes M\longrightarrow M\text{ is an equivalence for every }y,M. \] Here $M\in\mathcal C$, $K\otimes M=\colim_K M$, and the displayed map is induced by $F_y\to *$. Equivalently, $M\to M^{F_y}$ is an equivalence for every $M$. The assertion includes empty spaces and does not assume a symmetric monoidal structure on $\mathcal C$.
notes: Uses groupoid Kan formulas; does not silently assert the same for arbitrary derivators.

statement: Constant coefficients are tensor tests. For every $v:S\to T$ one has $v\in W_{\mathcal C}$ if and only if the canonical map $S\otimes M\to T\otimes M$ is an equivalence in $\mathcal C$ for every $M\in\mathcal C$.
notes: Includes empty and infinitely disconnected indexing spaces.

statement: The truncation calculation. Let $r\geq0$ be an integer and let $\mathcal C=\mathcal S_{\leq r}$ be the $\infty$-category of $r$-truncated spaces. Then \[ W_{\mathcal C}=W_r,\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_{r+1},\qquad W_{\mathcal C}^{\mathrm{coh}}=W_{\mathcal C}^{\mathrm{hom}}=W_{\mathcal C}^{1}. \] Membership in the common middle class is equivalent to \[ \pi_0v\text{ bijective},\qquad \pi_iv\text{ isomorphic }(1\leq i\leq r),\qquad \pi_{r+1}v\text{ onto}. \] The conditions on homotopy groups hold at every source point. For $r=0$ this includes sets, and for $r=1$ groupoids. The set-valued $W^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_1$ agrees with CATHOT C.1--C.4, which we cite without reproving its categorical-reflector statement.
notes: Sets and groupoids are r=0 and r=1. CATHOT reflector statement cited without reproof.

statement: Strictness and the failure of two-out-of-three. For every finite $r\geq0$, both inclusions $W_{r+1}\subset W_{\mathcal S_{\leq r}}^1\subset W_r$ are strict. The middle class does not satisfy two-out-of-three. For $\mathcal C=\mathcal S$, all five coefficient classes equal $W_\infty$.
notes: Explicit maps * -> K(A,r+1) -> *.

statement: Monodromy, with the algebra and the restriction specified. Let $k$ be an associative unital ring and let $(S,x)$ be a nonempty connected pointed space. Put $A_S=C_*(\Omega_xS;k)$, interpreted as the associative ring spectrum $Hk\wedge\Sigma^\infty_+\Omega_xS$, or the corresponding dg ring $k\otimes_{\Z}C_*(\Omega_xS;\Z)$; the loop operators commute with the $k$-action. There is an equivalence over $\Mod_k$ \[ \Fun(S,\Mod_k)\simeq \Mod_{A_S}, \] where evaluation at $x$ corresponds to forgetting the $A_S$-action. For a pointed map $v:(S,x)\to(T,y)$ the restriction functor corresponds to restriction of scalars along the specified algebra map $a_v:A_S\to A_T$. No finiteness, nilpotence, or simple-connectivity hypothesis is needed. This is the monadicity theorem \citep[Theorem 4.7.3.5]{EF_LurieHA} applied to evaluation; the compatible chain model is \citet[Corollary 9.2]{C_RiveraZeinalian2018}.
notes: No finite type, nilpotence, or simply connected restriction.

statement: All coefficient classes for an arbitrary ring. Suppose $k\ne0$. Then the following are exact descriptions of the indicated classes, for every map $v:S\to T$ of spaces represented by small categories: \begin{align*} v\in W_{D(k)} &\Longleftrightarrow H_j(S;k)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_j(T;k)\quad(j\geq0),\\ v\in W_{D(k)}^{\mathrm{coh}}=W_{D(k)}^{\mathrm{hom}}=W_{D(k)}^1 &\Longleftrightarrow H_0(F_y;k)\xrightarrow{\sim}k\text{ and }H_j(F_y;k)=0\quad(j>0,\ y\in T),\\ v\in W_{D(k)}^{\mathrm{lc}} &\Longleftrightarrow \begin{cases} \pi_0v\text{ bijective},\\ H_j(\Omega_xS;k)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_j(\Omega_{v(x)}T;k) \quad(j\geq0,\ x\in S), \end{cases}\\ &\Longleftrightarrow \begin{cases} \pi_0v\text{ bijective},\quad\pi_1(v,x)\text{ isomorphic},\\ H_j(\widetilde S_x;k)\xrightarrow{\sim}H_j(\widetilde T_{v(x)};k) \quad(j\geq0,\ x\in S). \end{cases} \end{align*} Here the last map is the lift determined by the chosen basepoints of the map on the corresponding connected components; it is equivariant for the specified isomorphism of fundamental groups. For $k=0$, every category of coefficients is terminal and every functor belongs to all five classes.
notes: Loop-algebra proof; integral bar/cobar followed by scalar extension; zero ring handled separately.

statement: The homological-epimorphism criterion and the point-target correction. For a pointed map of connected spaces, write $A=A_S$ and $B=A_T$. Then \[ v\in W_{D(k)}^1\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad B\otimes_A^{\mathbf L}B\xrightarrow{\mu}B\text{ is an equivalence of }B\text{-bimodules}. \] For every prederivator, irrespective of enhancement, a map $X\to e$ lies in $W_D$ if and only if it lies in $W_D^1$. Consequently the assertion in the CATHOT addendum that an acyclic-group map $BA\to e$ is not $1$-complete is false.
notes: Refutes the prompt assertion that BA -> * for acyclic A is not 1-complete; reversing the map gives the intended separation.

statement: Integral detection and arbitrary-ring arithmetic. Let $P(k)$ be the set of rational primes which are not units in a nonzero unital ring $k$. Each $k$-homology test in C.7 is equivalent to the simultaneous $\F_p$-homology tests for $p\in P(k)$, together with the $\Q$-homology test when $\operatorname{char}(k)=0$. In particular \[ W_{D(\Z)}^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_\infty, \qquad W_{D(k)}^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_\infty \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad P(k)\text{ contains every prime}. \]
notes: Includes all nonzero associative unital rings; integral Whitehead proof supplied.

statement: Spectra have the integral coefficient classes. For spectra, $W_{\Sp}$ is the class of integral homology equivalences, $W_{\Sp}^{\mathrm{coh}}=W_{\Sp}^{\mathrm{hom}}=W_{\Sp}^1$ is the class of maps with integrally acyclic homotopy fibres, and $W_{\Sp}^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_\infty$.
notes: Uses bounded-below stable Hurewicz detection only where it applies.

statement: A complete generalized-homology description for local spectra. Let $E$ be any nonzero spectrum, let $L_E\Sp$ denote Bousfield localization at $E$-homology equivalences, and use the associated derivator. Here $E_j(Z)=\pi_j(E\wedge\Sigma^\infty_+Z)$ is unreduced generalized homology. Then \begin{align*} W_{L_E\Sp}&=\{v:E_j(S)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_j(T)\ (j\in\Z)\},\\ W_{L_E\Sp}^{\mathrm{coh}}=W_{L_E\Sp}^{\mathrm{hom}}=W_{L_E\Sp}^{1} &=\{v:E\wedge\Sigma^\infty_+F_y\xrightarrow{\sim}E\ (y\in T)\},\\ W_{L_E\Sp}^{\mathrm{lc}} &=\{v:\pi_0v\text{ bijective and }E_j(\Omega_xS)\xrightarrow{\sim}E_j(\Omega_{v(x)}T) \ (j\in\Z,\ x\in S)\}. \end{align*} The last class forces isomorphisms of the discrete fundamental groups. These descriptions apply in particular to $E=K(n)$ at any prime and height $n\geq1$. For such $K(n)$ the last class strictly contains $W_\infty$. For $E=0$ all classes consist of every map.
notes: Nonzero E; zero E separately. For Morava K(n), Wlc strictly exceeds weak equivalences. No unsupported replacement of loop tests by cover tests.

statement: Strictness uniform in every nonzero ring and in spectra. For every nonzero unital ring $k$, both inclusions \[ W_{D(k)}^{\mathrm{lc}}\subsetneq W_{D(k)}^1\subsetneq W_{D(k)} \] are strict. The same is true for spectra. For $k=\Q$ or $k=\F_p$ one also has $W_\infty\subsetneq W_{D(k)}^{\mathrm{lc}}$. The first two strict inclusions hold for every nonzero coefficient $L_E\Sp$.
notes: Explicit acyclic presentation CW complex, finite A5 quotient, code/output, and corrected acyclic-group examples.

statement: The rational class is the established fibrewise rational class. For a map of connected pointed CW spaces, \[ v\in W_{D(\Q)}^{\mathrm{lc}} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \pi_1v\text{ is an isomorphism and } \pi_jv\otimes\Q\text{ is an isomorphism for every }j\geq2. \] Thus the class is that of $\pi_1$-rational homotopy equivalences, equivalently the maps inverted by fibrewise rationalization over $B\pi_1$. This characterization, including the cobar and local-coefficient formulations, is \citet[Theorem 3]{C_RiveraWierstraZeinalian2021}. For spaces whose universal covers have finite-dimensional rational homology in each degree, the algebraic models of \citet[Theorems 5.10, 5.11, 6.2, and 6.4]{C_GomezTatoHalperinTanre2000} model that fibrewise rational homotopy category. Their Definition 6.1 leaves the discrete fundamental group unchanged.
notes: Finite-type condition belongs to GHT models, not to the equivalence-class calculation.

statement: Schematization is a strictly weaker rational test. On connected pointed spaces, every map in $W_{D(\Q)}^{\mathrm{lc}}$ induces an equivalence of To\"en's schematizations over $\Q$, and the converse is false. The latter test requires an isomorphism of proalgebraic fundamental groups and cohomology isomorphisms for all finite-dimensional rational local systems, as in \citet[Lemma 3.3.2 and Theorem 3.3.4]{C_Toen2006}; its fundamental group is the proalgebraic completion, by Corollary 3.3.7 there. These assertions concern schematization of the specified map.
notes: Uncountable acyclic simple group supplies strictness; reverses a typo after Toën Definition3.1.1.

statement: The requested values, including their edge cases. The following table records the exact calculations. In the column headed ``middle'', the cohomological, homological, and $1$-complete classes coincide. ``Fibre $k$-acyclic'' means the augmented condition in C.7, ``cover $k$-equivalence'' includes bijectivity on $\pi_0$ and isomorphisms on $\pi_1$, and ``loop $E$-equivalence'' includes bijectivity on $\pi_0$. \begin{center} \small \begin{tabular}{>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{.18\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{.21\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{.27\textwidth}>{\raggedright\arraybackslash}p{.23\textwidth}} \hline Coefficient & Constant class & Middle class & $2$-complete class\\ \hline Sets & $W_0$ & $\pi_0$ bijective, $\pi_1$ onto & $W_1$\\ Groupoids & $W_1$ & $\pi_{\leq1}$ isomorphic, $\pi_2$ onto & $W_2$\\ $r$-types & $W_r$ & $\pi_{\leq r}$ isomorphic, $\pi_{r+1}$ onto & $W_{r+1}$\\ Spaces & $W_\infty$ & $W_\infty$ & $W_\infty$\\ $D(\Z)$ & Integral homology equivalences & Fibre $\Z$-acyclic & $W_\infty$\\ $D(\Q)$ & Rational homology equivalences & Fibre $\Q$-acyclic & Cover $\Q$-equivalence\\ $D(\F_p)$ & Mod-$p$ homology equivalences & Fibre $\F_p$-acyclic & Cover $\F_p$-equivalence\\ $D(k)$, $k\ne0$ & $k$-homology equivalences & Fibre $k$-acyclic & Cover $k$-equivalence\\ Spectra & Integral homology equivalences & Fibre $\Z$-acyclic & $W_\infty$\\ $L_E\Sp$, $E\ne0$ & $E$-homology equivalences & Fibre $E$-acyclic & Loop $E$-equivalence\\ Zero coefficients & Every map & Every map & Every map\\ \hline \end{tabular} \end{center}
notes: All requested coefficient cases included with the exact middle class.

statement: The two pullback tests are different. Fix a class $W$ of functors between small categories. A \emph{universal $W$-preserving map} is a functor $p:E\to B$ such that, for every functor $v:T'\to T$ over $B$ belonging to $W$, the induced functor \[ p^*v:E\times_B T'\longrightarrow E\times_B T \] belongs to $W$. All pullbacks in this definition are strict pullbacks in $\Cat$. This class of maps is closed under composition and arbitrary strict base change. It differs in general from the class obtained by testing only $T',T$ with weakly contractible nerves.
notes: No two-out-of-three assumption on W is needed for formal stability.

statement: What the local-coefficient repair actually proves. Let $\D$ satisfy the derivator axioms of Part A on all small categories, with the manuscript's presheaf variance. Suppose $p:E\to B$ has the following property after every strict base change: for each $M\in\D(e)$, $p_*M_E$ is locally constant and its evaluation at $b$ is canonically $H^*_{\D}(E_b,M)$. If $v:T'\to T$ is a $1$-complete equivalence over $B$, then \[ w:E\times_BT'\longrightarrow E\times_BT \] is a constant-coefficient $\D$-equivalence. The analogous statement with left Kan extensions holds. This does not assert that $w$ is $1$-complete or $2$-complete. If the direct-image hypothesis instead holds for every locally constant coefficient on every base-changed total category, then $v\in W^{\mathrm{coh}}_{\D}$ implies $w\in W^{\mathrm{coh}}_{\D}$. Such cohomological fibrations are closed under composition and base change; the dual assertion holds for homological fibrations. Under the enhancement hypotheses of C.2 these are universal $W^1_{\D}$-preserving fibrations.
depends_on: A inclusion chain; C.2 for enhanced equality
notes: The conclusion is not silently upgraded to Wlc. The dual homological argument is included.

statement: Composition for the manuscript's weak rational fibrations. For $\D=D(\Q)$ there are finite categories and functors $E\xrightarrow{p}B\xrightarrow{q}[1]$ such that $p$ and $q$ are the universal weak fibrations of I~ms.~117, while $qp$ is not one. Thus I-b-B081-04 is false, as is the unqualified composition claim at I~ms.~118.
depends_on: exact invariants of finite groups over Q
notes: Five arrows in intermediate category; ten in total; endpoint fibre component counts 2 and1.

statement: The restricted $2$-complete fibration condition still fails composition. Let $\D(A)=\Fun(A^{\op},\Set)$. Call $p:E\to B$ a restricted $2$-complete fibration if, for every $v:T'\to T$ over $B$ with $BT'$ and $BT$ weakly contractible, $E\times_BT'\to E\times_BT$ belongs to $W^{\mathrm{lc}}_{\D}=W_1$. There are finite $E\xrightarrow{p}B\xrightarrow{q}[1]$ for which both factors have this property and the composite does not. The first factor is a $\Hot$-fibration; the second is even a universal $W_1$-equivalence. Consequently this is a counterexample to the replacement ``$2$-complete throughout'' in Lead~3, including its composition assertion.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: I ms122 composition development; Lead3 blanket substitution
notes: Nonzero normalized C2 cocycle on barycentric S2; all categorical laws and pi1 presentations checked.

statement: Total equivalence need not detect fibres after either blanket substitution. The following two assertions are false. First, a $2$-complete equivalence between $\Hot$-fibrations over a completely $\D$-aspherical base must be $2$-complete on every strict fibre. Second, a $1$-complete equivalence between universal $W^1_{\D}$-preserving fibrations must be $1$-complete on every fibre. Both failures occur for set-valued coefficients. In contrast, under the enhancement hypotheses of C.2, a $1$-complete equivalence between $\Hot$-fibrations over the same base is $1$-complete on every fibre.
notes: Counterexamples include a completely Set-aspherical base and a contractible base respectively.

statement: A fibration class with the requested stability and fibre detection. Assume $W=W^{\mathrm{lc}}_{\D}$ is an accessible fundamental localizer. Equip $\Cat$ with the Thomason model structure associated to $W$, whose existence is \citet[Theorem 5.2.15]{Cisinski2006}. Its fibrations are closed under arbitrary strict base change and composition. If $p:E\to S$ and $q:F\to S$ are such fibrations and $f:E\to F$ is a functor over $S$ belonging to $W$, then $f_s:E_s\to F_s$ belongs to $W$ for every object $s\in S$. Right properness of the model structure is not needed for this assertion.
notes: Right properness unnecessary for the slice-fibrant fibre-detection assertion; model fibrations not identified with all sharp maps.

statement: Universal constant equivalences control arbitrary coefficients. Let $\D$ be a derivator on all small categories with both pointwise homotopy Kan extensions, pointwise detection, and the disjoint-union axiom. If every strict pullback of $u:A\to B$ is a constant-coefficient $\D$-equivalence, then $u^*:\D(B)\to\D(A)$ is fully faithful. In particular this holds if every strict pullback of $u$ is $1$-complete or $2$-complete. Thus I-b-B084-01 is affirmative under these hypotheses, without an enhancement assumption.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: I-b-B084-01; I ms82 arbitrary inverse-image fibre formula
notes: Full factorization-category mate proof, including infinite or empty hom-sets.

statement: The HOT conclusions and the weak-contractible-base equivalence. For the homotopy derivator of spaces, all five equivalence classes of Part A equal $W_\infty$. The universal weak cohomological fibration condition, its homological counterpart, the test on every map between weakly contractible bases, and universal preservation of $W_\infty$ are equivalent. This settles I-b-B096-04 for the usual derivator axioms and settles Ib-C021, Ib-C026, Ib-C048, Ib-C069, Ib-C092 and Ib-C096 in the modern HOT setting. For a general derivator, the weak-contractible-base test is equivalent to the two universal weak conditions under Der~3~$a'$; the latter axiom follows from \citet[Corollary 3.8]{Cisinski2009LocallyConstant}.
depends_on: Cisinski2009 Corollary3.8; Quillen1973 TheoremB; Rezk1998 Proposition2.7
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: I-b-B096-04; Ib-C021; Ib-C026; Ib-C048; Ib-C069; Ib-C092; Ib-C096; XI opening
notes: General derivator argument provided separately from HOT identification.

statement: Errors not removed by changing the equivalence class. The uniqueness assertion I-b-B087-05, the two implications I-b-B093-04 and I-b-B093-05, the orbit relations I-b-B095-01, the properness assertion Ib-C003, and the internal-Hom assertion Ib-C082 are false as stated. Their corrections are independent of a wholesale replacement by $W^{\mathrm{lc}}_{\D}$.
notes: Corrected orbit compositions and quotient rational Betti vector (1,0,0,1) are checked.

statement: The doubled-arrow test and the scope of the repair. For the space derivator, the doubled-arrow construction of I-b-A069 cannot produce the proposed failure of weak cohomological fibration. The same gluing step is valid for $W^{\mathrm{lc}}_{\D}$ and $W^1_{\D}$ when $\D$ has the complete enhanced coefficient category of C.1. This statement concerns that specified base change only.
depends_on: homotopy pushout of simplicial monomorphisms; C.1
notes: One specified fork base change; no claim that all base changes preserve the original weak condition.

statement: The doubled-arrow generalization for every derivator. Let $\D$ satisfy Der~1--4 on all small categories. If a cosieve inclusion $i:X_1\to X$ belongs to $W^{\mathrm{lc}}_{\D}$, then both copy inclusions $X\to X\amalg_{X_1}X$ belong to $W^{\mathrm{lc}}_{\D}$. Consequently the strengthened $2$-complete gluing step in the specified doubled-arrow construction is valid without an enhancement. The corresponding $1$-complete gluing step is also valid, by B.5.
depends_on: B.3 arbitrary-derivator relative Theorem A; B.5 direct excision; Cisinski2006 Theorems1.4.3 and4.2.15
notes: The former general descent gap is resolved. Wlc gluing uses the accessible fundamental sublocalizer generated by the single cosieve inclusion; no accessibility assumption on all Wlc is needed. W1 uses B.5 Loc6a.

statement: The original claim already fails for $0$-type coefficients. For $\D(A)=\Fun(A^{\op},\Set)$, a universal weak cohomological and homological fibration need not preserve constant-coefficient equivalences. Thus the truncated-type qualification I-b-B079-07, as well as I-b-B079-03 and I-b-B079-04, is false in degree zero.
notes: e→BC2 preserves pi0; pullback G_disc→EG changes pi0.

statement: What ``one categorical level up'' means. Let $\mathcal C$ be an $\infty$-category, small in a universe $\V$ larger than the universe $\U$ of indexing spaces. Put \[ K_0(\mathcal C)=\mathcal C^{\simeq},\qquad K_1(\mathcal C)=\Fun(\Delta^1,\mathcal C)^{\simeq}. \] For a map $f:X\to Y$ of $\U$-small spaces, restriction $f^*:\Fun(Y,\mathcal C)\to\Fun(X,\mathcal C)$ is an equivalence if and only if both canonical maps \[ \Map(Y,K_i(\mathcal C))\longrightarrow\Map(X,K_i(\mathcal C)), \qquad i=0,1, \] are equivalences of spaces. This is a two-object orthogonality description, not by itself the constant-coefficient class of a derivator. If $\mathcal C$ is locally $\U$-small and admits the required $\U$-small cotensors, equivalence of the ordinary homotopy categories under the specified restriction functor is equivalent to the stated $\infty$-categorical condition. The same conclusion holds without local $\U$-smallness whenever that restriction has a Kan-extension adjoint.
notes: Two test objects do not alone construct a derivator.

statement: An ordinary derivator realization for linear coefficients. Fix universes $\U\subset\V\subset\mathcal W$, and an $\U$-small $E_\infty$-ring spectrum $R$. Let $\mathcal P_R$ denote the $\infty$-category of $\U$-presentable $R$-linear stable $\infty$-categories and $R$-linear colimit-preserving functors. We regard it as a category in the larger universes; all limits and colimits required below have $\U$-small shapes. Let \[ \D_R(A)=\Ho\Fun(NA^{\op},\Mod_R),\qquad \D'_R(A)=\Ho\Fun(NA^{\op},\mathcal P_R). \] Both are derivators on $\Cat_\U$, and their classes of functors satisfy \[ W_{\D'_R}=W_{\D_R}^{\mathrm{lc}}. \tag{E.2.1} \] Thus the equality in Part E has an ordinary-derivator realization for commutative rings, by taking $R=Hk$. It uses the specified symmetric monoidal enhancement of $\D_R$. It is functorial in maps of $E_\infty$-rings by extension of scalars; it is not an assignment constructed from an arbitrary unadorned derivator.
notes: Specified monoidal enhancement; all small indexing shapes; larger coefficient universes; zero ring included.

statement: The two-categorical version of the linear realization. Retain the hypotheses of E.2, and retain the full $\infty$-categories of natural transformations between $R$-linear left adjoints. The class of maps $f:X\to Y$ for which all restrictions \[ \Fun\bigl(Y,\Fun_R^L(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)\bigr) \longrightarrow \Fun\bigl(X,\Fun_R^L(\mathcal A,\mathcal B)\bigr) \tag{E.3.1} \] are equivalences is also $W_{\D_R}^{\mathrm{lc}}$. The same is true if equivalence in (E.3.1) is tested on ordinary homotopy categories. These are the Hom-category constant tests in the coefficient $(\infty,2)$-category $\mathcal P_R$. No assertion that its diagram assignment satisfies every axiom of Di Vittorio's 2-derivators is needed for this equality.
notes: Does not assert every HDer axiom for an enriched-shape extension.

statement: A specified second linear stage detects degree-two torsion. For $R=H\Q$ use the particular coefficient category $\mathcal P_\Q$ of E.2, and define \[ W_{\Q}^{(2)}=W_{\D'_\Q}^{\mathrm{lc}},\qquad W_{\Q}^{(1)}=W_{\D_\Q}^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_{\D'_\Q}. \] For every prime $p$, the projection $K(\Z/p,2)\to *$ is not in $W_{\Q}^{(2)}$. The projection $K(\Z,2)\to *$ is not in that class either. The first projection is in $W_{\Q}^{(1)}$, so the inclusion $W_{\Q}^{(2)}\subset W_{\Q}^{(1)}$ is strict.
notes: Uses units in Q(zeta_p), and powers of 2 in Q.

statement: The explicitly specified tower starting with sets. For $r\ge0$ put $\mathcal C_r=\mathcal S_{\le r}$ and let $\D_r$ be its derivator. Then \[ W_{\D_r}=W_r,\qquad W_{\D_r}^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_{r+1},\qquad \bigcap_{r\ge0}W_r=W_\infty. \tag{E.5.1} \] Consequently the stipulated choice $\mathcal C_r\mapsto \mathcal C_{r+1}$ realizes the descending tower in Lead 4 for sets. It does not characterize a unique coefficient-raising operation.
notes: Does not characterize a canonical raising operation on arbitrary derivators.

statement: What the attached 2-derivator paper actually proves. In arXiv:2309.05216v2, Di Vittorio's shapes are small simplicially enriched categories, and a 2-prederivator is a trihomomorphism $\mathrm{Dia}^{\op}\to\mathrm{GRAY}$, not a prederivator on ordinary $\Cat$ alone. For the 2-prederivator of a combinatorial $\mathrm{sSet}_{\mathrm{Joyal}}$-enriched model category, axioms (HDer 1)--(HDer 4) are proved, whereas (HDer 5) is Conjecture 3.2.23. All five axioms, when assumed, are preserved by shift.
manuscript_rows_or_pages_settled: Recent results; Part E and G
notes: Shift invariance of all five assumed axioms is proved; enriched shapes differ from ordinary Cat.

statement: A conditional realization by localized spaces. Let $\mathcal L\subset\mathcal S$ be an accessible reflective localization with reflector $L$, and let $W$ be the maps inverted by $L$. Assume $W$ is preserved by product with every small space. For the derivator $\D_{\mathcal L}$ of $\mathcal L$, its constant-coefficient class is $W$. In particular, if $W_\D^{\mathrm{lc}}$ is accessible as a fundamental localizer, there exists a derivator of localized spaces $\D^{\mathrm{loc}}$ with \[ W_{\D^{\mathrm{loc}}}=W_\D^{\mathrm{lc}}. \] The construction is functorial for specified inclusions between accessible fundamental localizers. By B.4, the accessibility hypothesis holds whenever $\D$ is the derivator of a $\U$-presentable infinity-category.
notes: Uses product stability and Cisinski2006 Theorems4.2.15,1.4.3; unrestricted derivator-morphism functoriality is not asserted.

statement: The complete second-stage loop criterion. Let $R\ne0$ be an $E_\infty$-ring spectrum, and put $W_R^{(2)}=W_{\D'_R}^{\mathrm{lc}}$ for the realization in E.2. A map $f:X\to Y$ of $\U$-small spaces is in $W_R^{(2)}$ if and only if it is bijective on components and, for one basepoint $x$ in every component, the specified map \[ \Omega_xf:\Omega_xX\longrightarrow\Omega_{f(x)}Y \] belongs to $W_{\D_R}^{\mathrm{lc}}$. In particular, for a nonzero commutative ordinary ring $k$, \[ f\in W_k^{(2)} \quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} \pi_0(f)\text{ is bijective},\\ \pi_1(f),\pi_2(f)\text{ are isomorphisms at every basepoint},\\ H_*(X\langle2\rangle;k)\longrightarrow H_*(Y\langle2\rangle;k)\text{ is an isomorphism on each component}. \end{cases} \tag{E.8.1} \] Here $X\langle2\rangle$ is the homotopy fibre at the chosen basepoint of $X\to\tau_{\le2}X$; all maps of covers are the ones induced by $f$ and the chosen basepoints. This is a full computation of the specified rational second stage on taking $k=\Q$, with no nilpotence or finite-type assumption on $X$ or $Y$. In that case the last condition is equivalently that $\pi_j(f)\otimes\Q$ is an isomorphism for every $j\ge3$; the 2-connected covers to which rational Whitehead applies are automatically simply connected.
notes: For Q equivalently exact pi0/pi1/pi2 and rational higher homotopy. Uses canonical free-linear-presheaf algebra map and monadicity, including disconnected loops.

statement: Degree-three torsion survives the second rational stage. For every prime $p$, the projection $K(\Z/p,3)\to *$ belongs to the specific $W_\Q^{(2)}$ of E.4. More generally this holds for every nonempty, 2-connected, rationally acyclic space in place of $K(\Z/p,3)$. In particular \[ W_\infty\subsetneq W_\Q^{(2)} \subsetneq W_\Q^{(1)}. \]
notes: Independent Postnikov proof; both coefficient core and arrow core have rational homotopy groups above degree two.

statement: A rational loop tower and its ordinary coefficient realization. Define the following specified tower of classes of maps of spaces: \[ V_0=W_{\D_\Q},\qquad V_{r+1}=\{f:X\to Y\mid \pi_0(f)\text{ is bijective and } \Omega_xf\in V_r\text{ for every component}\}. \tag{E.10.1} \] For $r\ge1$ its exact description is \[ f\in V_r\quad\Longleftrightarrow\quad \begin{cases} \pi_0(f)\text{ is bijective},\\ \pi_i(f)\text{ is an isomorphism }(1\le i\le r),\\ \pi_j(f)\otimes\Q\text{ is an isomorphism }(j>r). \end{cases} \tag{E.10.2} \] The rationalization condition concerns the higher abelian homotopy groups and their specified maps. We have $V_1=W_\Q^{(1)}$, $V_2=W_\Q^{(2)}$ for the actual coefficient categories constructed above, strict inclusions $V_{r+1}\subsetneq V_r$ for every $r\ge0$, and $\bigcap_{r\ge0}V_r=W_\infty$. Every $V_r$ is an accessible fundamental localizer. For $r\ge1$ let $\mathcal C_r=\mathcal S_{V_r}$ be its category of local spaces, and write $\D_r=\D_{\mathcal C_r}$, with $\D_0=\D_\Q$. These are a specified tower of ordinary derivators satisfying \[ W_{\D_r}=V_r, \qquad W_{\D_r}^{\mathrm{lc}}=V_{r+1} \quad(r\ge0). \tag{E.10.3} \] One may instead use $\D_1=\D'_\Q$ from E.2 and retain $\D_r=\D_{\mathcal C_r}$ for $r\ge2$; the same equalities hold. Thus the tower, including its intersection, has a construction by ordinary coefficient categories. The stages $\mathcal C_r$ are localized spaces; they are not identified here with categories of higher $\Q$-linear categories. More generally, if an initial derivator $\mathbb E$ has accessible $W_{\mathbb E}^{\mathrm{lc}}\subseteq W_0$, the same repeated localized-space realization constructs an ordinary coefficient tower whose intersection is $W_\infty$. In particular this applies to every nonterminal $\U$-presentable infinity-category coefficient.
notes: Includes every nonterminal presentable initial coefficient. The first linear coefficient category may be retained; later localized-space coefficients are not asserted to be higher linear categories.

statement: Arbitrary bare-derivator functoriality and higher linear coefficients. For an arbitrary derivator on $\Cat_\U$ we have not constructed a functorial assignment $\D\mapsto\D'$ with $W_{\D'}=W_\D^{\mathrm{lc}}$. A phrase such as ``$\D$-linear categories'' does not specify such an assignment without a monoidal enhancement and a choice of morphisms. E.2 settles a specified enhanced linear case, and B.4 together with E.7 gives a realizing derivator of localized spaces for every presentable infinity-category coefficient. Neither proves a functorial assignment on all bare derivators and all their morphisms. The full second linear stage is computed in E.8, and E.10 constructs an entire ordinary coefficient tower with its stated intersection. A realization of its further stages by higher $\Q$-linear categories, with a specified higher monodromy construction and morphism class, remains unresolved here.
notes: Full ordinary tower and its intersection are constructed; only higher linear-categorical realization remains separate.

statement: All-set fibre functors recover the fundamental groupoid. Let $X$ be a $\U$-small space, let $G=\Pi_1X$, and retain the ordinary category $\mathcal L_0(X)=\Fun(G,\Set_\U)$ together with its evaluation functors $\omega_x:\mathcal L_0(X)\to\Set_\U$ for a set of points meeting every component. The category whose objects are these functors and whose arrows are all natural transformations between them is a groupoid equivalent to $G$. With every point retained, the comparison is the specified fully faithful functor \[ x\longmapsto\omega_x, \qquad \Hom_G(x,y)\longrightarrow \operatorname{Nat}(\omega_x,\omega_y). \tag{F.1.1} \] Restricting instead to finite sets recovers the profinite Galois invariant; it must not be identified with the full groupoid in (F.1.1).
notes: Yoneda reconstruction; empty and disconnected cases included; CATHOT reflector cited without reproof.

statement: Enhanced linear reconstruction with a specified fibre. Let $R$ be an $E_\infty$-ring spectrum and $(X,x)$ a pointed connected $\U$-small space. Retain the $R$-linear stable $\infty$-category \[ \mathcal L_R(X)=\Fun(X,\Mod_R) \] and its $R$-linear evaluation functor $\omega_x:\mathcal L_R(X)\to\Mod_R$, including its coherent functor structure. This pair determines the $E_1$-algebra $R[\Omega_xX]$ up to equivalence of $E_1$-algebras. For an ordinary commutative ring $k$ and $R=Hk$, it determines $C_*(\Omega_xX;k)$ as an associative derived $k$-algebra, with the prescribed variance convention. Retaining fibres in every component gives the corresponding many-object linear path category.
notes: Recover the specified algebra via the evaluation monad, not only a Morita class.

statement: Spaces are recovered from enhanced space-valued local systems. For every $\U$-small space $X$, the $\infty$-topos $\mathcal L_{\mathcal S}(X)=\Fun(X,\mathcal S_\U)$ has shape the constant pro-space $X$. Retaining its evaluation functors $\omega_x$ and their full spaces of natural transformations recovers $X$ as an $\infty$-groupoid. Retaining only the homotopy category still suffices if, in addition, the specified constant functor $\Ho\mathcal S\to\Ho\mathcal L_{\mathcal S}(X)$ is retained: in that case one recovers the object $X$ of $\Hot$ by Yoneda.
notes: Known shape construction, independently proved; constant functor is additional named datum in ordinary formulation.

statement: The form applicable to a locally connected topos. Let $\mathcal E$ be a locally connected Grothendieck topos, and let $\Pi_1\mathcal E$ be its fundamental pro-groupoid, equivalently the 1-truncation of the shape of its associated $\infty$-topos. There is a canonical equivalence \[ \Fun(\Pi_1\mathcal E,\Set) \simeq\LC_{\Set}(\mathcal E). \tag{F.4.1} \] For a representing cofiltered diagram $(G_i)$, the left side means the filtered colimit of the categories $\Fun(G_i,\Set)$ in the sense of representations of a pro-groupoid; it is not the category of actions of the abstract inverse-limit group with its topology forgotten. The full subcategory of filtered colimits of locally constant objects is the corresponding classifying topos. In particular, if $\mathcal E$ is generated under colimits by its locally constant objects, the canonical map $\mathcal E\to\beta(\Pi_1\mathcal E)$ is an equivalence.
notes: Hoyois Thm3.13 and Cor3.20; retains covering-family data; no unsupported claim LC always a topos.

statement: Kaledin's groupoid enhancement already reconstructs spaces. For a small space $X$ consider the family \[ J\longmapsto\Pi_1\Map(BJ,X). \tag{F.5.1} \] Kaledin's enhanced-groupoid representability theorem identifies the appropriate small families satisfying his axioms with homotopy types. More precisely, in the attached arXiv:2409.17489v3, Definition 6.1.1.3 and Corollary 6.1.2.5 give the groupoid case; Theorem 7.3.1.3 is the more general representability theorem for enhanced categories. Thus the reconstruction of a space from (F.5.1), with all the structure required there, is already recorded in the literature.
notes: Exact Pos and Pos+ shapes and uncountable regular size bounds retained; Chapters6-7 preliminary.

statement: The relation between the coefficient tower and varying shapes. The finite-type tower in E.5 and the family (F.5.1) both determine $X$ up to equivalence, but their parameters and their truncations are different. The tower raises the coefficient category at fixed $X$. Kaledin fixes the target of the reported values to ordinary groupoids and varies the source shape $J$, retaining all coherence between those values. In general \[ \Pi_1\Map(BJ,X)\not\simeq \Map(BJ,\Pi_1X), \tag{F.6.1} \] even on components. The explicit comparison from enhanced space-valued local systems is obtained by first forming the full $\infty$-groupoid of designated fibre functors in F.3 and then taking $\Pi_1\Fun(BJ,-)$ of that groupoid.
notes: Finite tetrahedral face poset and K(Z,2) witness; exact program output attached.

statement: A precise recognition question for a coefficient theory. For a complete coefficient $\infty$-category $\mathcal C$, the condition $W_{\mathcal C}^{\mathrm{lc}}=W_\infty$ means that the contravariant functor $X\mapsto\Fun(X,\mathcal C)$ reflects equivalences of \emph{specified maps} of spaces. Equivalently, the pair of test spaces $K_0(\mathcal C),K_1(\mathcal C)$ of E.1 detects all weak equivalences. In the cases computed in Part C, this holds for spaces, integral derived coefficients, and spectra; it fails for sets, groupoids, every fixed finite truncation level, rational derived coefficients, and mod-$p$ derived coefficients.
notes: General rings and E-local spectra inherit qualifications from Part C.

statement: The reconstruction problem with only ordinary fibre functors. If the input in Part F is restricted literally to the ordinary category $\LC_{\D_R}(X)$ and ordinary functors $\LC_{\D_R}(X)\to\D_R(e)$, with no enhanced mapping objects, no coherent adjunction data, and no specified family of shifted categories, F.2 does not establish reconstruction of the $E_1$-algebra $C_*(\Omega X;k)$. We leave that unenhanced assertion unresolved. Likewise F.3 without either its $\infty$-topos structure or its specified constant functor does not establish the corresponding bare-category assertion.
notes: Exact gap is recovery of coherent monad data; not presented as a counterexample.

statement: Locally constant coefficients detect components for every nontrivial derivator. Let $\D$ be a derivator on all $\U$-small categories. If $\D(e)$ is not equivalent to the terminal category, then \[ \Wlc\subseteq\W_0. \tag{G.1.1} \] If $\D(e)\simeq e$, then $\D(A)\simeq e$ for every $A$, and all five classes consist of every functor. Thus the hypothesis is exact.
notes: Nonterminal point coefficients are necessary and sufficient for Wlc subset W0; no enhancement.

statement: The exact obstruction for constant coefficients. For a derivator, $\Wc\subseteq\W_0$ holds if and only if $\D(e)$ is not a preorder up to equivalence. More explicitly, if there exist two distinct parallel morphisms $\alpha,\beta:M\to N$ in $\D(e)$, then every constant-coefficient equivalence is bijective on components. If $\D(e)$ is a nontrivial preorder up to equivalence, then \[ \Wc=\{f:A\to B:\ A\text{ and }B\text{ are both empty or both nonempty}\}. \tag{G.2.1} \] In particular, Chapter X's component-detection expectation needs a coefficient-separation hypothesis for $\Wc$, but only nontriviality for $\Wlc$.
notes: Constant component detection iff nonthin point category. Nontrivial preorder constants detect only emptiness.

statement: What an arbitrary morphism of derivators supplies. A pseudonatural morphism $\Phi:\D\to\mathbf E$ restricts to functors $\Phi_A:\LC_\D(A)\to\LC_{\mathbf E}(A)$, coherently commuting with restriction. This alone imposes no inclusion in either direction between $\W_\D^{\mathrm{lc}}$ and $\W_{\mathbf E}^{\mathrm{lc}}$. Equivalence of derivators gives equality of the five classes. Products give intersections of the five classes.
notes: Arbitrary derivator morphisms give no direction of class inclusion; equivalences and products treated separately.

statement: Retracts and fully faithful comparisons. If $\mathbf E$ is a pseudoretract of $\D$, namely if there are morphisms $\Phi:\D\to\mathbf E$ and $\Psi:\mathbf E\to\D$ with $\Phi\Psi\cong\id$, then \[ \W_\D^{\mathrm{lc}}\subseteq\W_{\mathbf E}^{\mathrm{lc}}, \qquad \W_\D^1\subseteq\W_{\mathbf E}^1, \qquad \W_\D\subseteq\W_{\mathbf E}. \tag{G.4.1} \] If instead every $\Phi_A$ is fully faithful, then $\W_{\mathbf E}^1\subseteq\W_\D^1$ and $\W_{\mathbf E}\subseteq\W_\D$. To infer the analogous assertion for $2$-completeness one additionally needs descent of the essential image: whenever $F\in\LC_\D(A)$ and $G\in\LC_{\mathbf E}(B)$ satisfy $f^*G\cong\Phi_A F$, an object $G$ with this property must be choosable in the essential image of $\Phi_B$.
notes: Pseudoretract and fully faithful coefficient comparisons; essential-image descent explicitly required for equivalences.

statement: Change of scalars and the Chapter X assignment. Let $k\to l$ be a homomorphism of associative unital rings. Derived extension of scalars gives \[ \W_{D(k)}^{\mathrm{lc}}\subseteq\W_{D(l)}^{\mathrm{lc}}, \qquad \W_{D(k)}\subseteq\W_{D(l)}. \tag{G.5.1} \] The first inclusion is equality if derived extension of scalars reflects equivalences and the canonical loop-algebra comparison can be reflected by it; in particular this holds for a faithfully flat map of nonzero commutative rings. Thus $\D\mapsto\Wlc$ is well defined on equivalence classes of derivators and has precise functoriality under additional hypotheses, but is not monotone on all morphisms of derivators.
notes: Unital associative rings; scalar extension inclusion, faithfully flat commutative reflection, and zero-ring cases.

statement: A functorial higher-coefficient construction on bare derivators. For an arbitrary derivator $\D$ with no specified monoidal enhancement, this work does not construct a functorially assigned derivator $\D'$ with $\W_{\D'}=\Wlc$, nor an iteratable $2$-derivator construction of that kind. The requested general statement is retained with those quantifiers. A chosen presentable linear enhancement has the positive realization in E.2; a specified accessible space localization has the conditional realization in E.7. The missing data in the general proposal are a category of $\D$-linear categories, its morphisms and coherent $2$-morphisms, and Kan extensions on the enriched shapes required by Di Vittorio. The full relative Theorem A for arbitrary derivators is proved in B.3. That localizer theorem by itself does not specify an iteratable coefficient category or the required enriched shapes.
notes: All-bare-derivator functorial coefficient raising and iteratable enriched 2-derivator enhancement remain unspecified; accessible localized-space realization is proved.
